title: Forsyth County Sheriff establishes first U.S. A2Z AirDock network, expanding drone-as-first-responder capabilities
summary: A2Z Drone Delivery’s multi-mission drone dock network is designed to complement the department’s growing DFR drone capabilities as a holistic integrated platform supporting search and rescue, criminal investigations, and enhanced situational awareness for service calls.
body_markdown:
[A2Z Drone Delivery, Inc.](https://www.a2zdronedelivery.com/) , a California-based aerospace and engineering company advancing commercial unmanned aerial vehicles, today announced that the[Forsyth County Sheriff’s Office](https://forsyth.cc/sheriff/) (FCSO) has launched the nation’s first[A2Z AirDock](https://www.a2zdronedelivery.com/airdock-drone-infrastructure) network. A dedicated network for drone-as-first-responder (DFR) missions, the infrastructure supports a fleet of[A2Z Longtail Patrol](https://www.a2zdronedelivery.com/longtail-delivery-drone) drones, adding new aerial capabilities to the department’s law enforcement toolkit and laying the foundation for expanding the agency’s use of autonomous drone technology across multiple use cases. For more information about this first-of-its-kind DFR network, please visit:[https://www.a2zdronedelivery.com/drones-as-first-responder](https://www.a2zdronedelivery.com/drones-as-first-responder) .


The first A2Z AirDock installments enable the FCSO drone team to reach a service area of up to 200 square miles in the region surrounding Winston-Salem, NC. With the A2Z commercial drone delivery winch factory-integrated alongside a comprehensive first-responder payload of imaging sensors, LED light, and megaphone, the Longtail Patrol is capable of far more than simply being “eyes in the sky” for first responders.


Combining these payload capabilities with the A2Z AirDocks enables the purpose-built drone fleet to be forward-stationed throughout the area of operation for rapid deployment in support of calls for service. Automatically recharging the Longtail aircraft between calls, the dock network is already impacting rapid police-call response, repeatable search-and-rescue operations, criminal investigations, and emergency delivery of automated external defibrillators (AEDs). In its initial few weeks of operation, the program has flown more than 500 miles over 25 flight hours.


The combined network of DFR drones and charging docks builds on the Sheriff’s Office’s ongoing leadership in the deployment of drone assets in support of its law enforcement operations. By combining A2Z’s multi-mission Longtail aircraft, payload delivery technology, and automated docking infrastructure, Forsyth County is laying the foundation for a distributed drone network designed to support a range of public safety applications that can easily expand to meet new multi-mission use cases.


“Drone as first responder technology gives us another tool to help protect our community, provide deputies with critical information sooner, and reach people who need assistance,” said Forsyth County Sheriff Bobby Kimbrough Jr. “With these A2Z AirDocks in place, we can continue exploring how autonomous drone technology can strengthen our response capabilities, support search-and-rescue operations, and help get lifesaving equipment like AEDs to the field when every minute matters.”


**Establishing a Network for Rapid Public Safety Response**


The first three erected AirDock stations represent a significant step in extending the Sheriff’s Office’s drone capabilities beyond individual launch locations. By positioning automated drone infrastructure at strategic sites, the aerial assets are pre-deployed closer to the areas they serve, reducing the operational burden of deploying and servicing drones across a broad geographic area. Using a common infrastructure network for these missions offers the Sheriff’s Office a pathway to expand drone operations without necessarily requiring a separate aircraft and dedicated launch site for every application.


“Sheriff Kimbrough and the Forsyth County Sheriff’s drone team have long been at the forefront of DFR implementation, and with this first deployment of our A2Z AirDock technology in the United States for public safety use cases, they are demonstrating how dedicated DFR systems can evolve from individual aircraft deployments into an aerial public safety network,” said Aaron Zhang, CEO of A2Z Drone Delivery. “Forsyth County has established a foundation that is demonstrating how autonomous multi-mission aircraft can support a wider range of emergency response operations. From providing aerial intelligence to delivering lifesaving equipment, a single drone platform can give public safety teams more ways to put drone technology to work in service of its residents and businesses.”


**Automated Docking Infrastructure Reduces Operational Burden**


A key component of the Forsyth County deployment is A2Z’s AirDock automated drone infrastructure, which supports autonomous drone launch, recovery, and charging. Designed to operate remotely, the stations eliminate the need for personnel to travel to each launch location, manually exchange batteries, or remain physically present to service aircraft between missions. The A2Z AirDocks are designed with no moving parts in order to minimize maintenance and increase the reliability of aircraft availability to responding teams. This “solid state” design also minimizes the infrastructure investment for each dock, allowing the reach of the network to scale more feasibly over time


For public safety agencies, these capabilities address a central challenge in scaling DFR operations: expanding geographic coverage while managing staffing and operational demands. Corporal John Lasley, who leads the Forsyth County Sheriff’s Office drone team, has previously highlighted the operational advantages of A2Z’s automated docking technology, particularly for missions in remote locations.


“The AirDock is another game changer because it allows us to fly to remote locations without needing a person there to service the drone,” said Lasley. “Something that drone operators often forget about when setting up operations is just how many hands-on people you actually need for these missions. The AirDocks drastically reduce the manpower needed for the whole operation.”


A2Z’s Longtail aircraft are designed for multi-mission operations, allowing agencies to use a common platform for delivering payloads up to 8.8 lbs. to the field of operation, and also conduct aerial observation flights to 12.4 miles of range without an added payload below the drone winch. When equipped with A2Z’s RDS2 commercial drone delivery winch, the aircraft can lower and deposit payloads from altitude without landing. This keeps spinning propellers away from people, property, and potential ground-level obstructions during delivery.


For investigative missions, search-and-rescue, or to provide officers in the field with improved situational awareness, the Longtail aircraft are also equipped with multiple imaging sensors, including a high-res optical zoom camera and a thermal imaging sensor for locating heat signatures in the dark. The customizable payload bay also carries a powerful LED light for illuminating response scenes, and a megaphone that enables officers to communicate with people on the ground.


“As Forsyth County continues developing its drone operations, the combination of automated docking stations, multi-mission aircraft, and payload delivery capabilities offers a pathway to broaden the role of drones in public safety while helping manage the personnel and infrastructure required to sustain these services,” said Zhang. “Our AirDocks are also designed to be sharable between multiple stakeholders, so as the high-priority use cases such as DFR reach further throughout the county, the multi-drone docks maintain sufficient capacity for other municipal departments to layer aerial drone services onto the same dock infrastructure. This unique opportunity means other municipal departments can operate complementary drone routes in parallel to the daily DFR missions at a fraction of the cost of standing up independent operations.”
